$comment: Erudite feature list. Written in Phase 3, confirmed at Gate 3.
Copy to <project>\feature_list.json.
APPEND ONLY. Never edit an id, category, description or steps once written.
Never delete a feature. The ONLY permitted change is passes false -> true.
Flip passes only when evidence.command was run and evidence.output holds
what it actually printed. RULES.md 7-12.
FAILURES.md F9: thirteen of twenty-two progress rows were found wrong
because they were ticked from recollection of having done the work.
FAILURES.md F8: a green tick from a command that inspected zero files.
If a feature turns out to be wrong, add a NEW one and leave the old one
failing. A passing count that drops is a failure, not a pass.
Every feature is END-TO-END and USER-VISIBLE - something a person can do,
screen to database and back. Not a layer. Not 'create the users table'.
Every feature is written so it can be proven FALSE.
evidence_file names the file under <project>\evidence\ that backs the tick,
e.g. "evidence\\F002.txt". verify-gate.ps1 does NOT read it - it reads
evidence.command and evidence.output - so it changes no behaviour. It is here
so a tick can be traced to a file by machine and not only by memory. Leave it
as an empty string until the feature is proven.
category is one of: auth, data, ui, reporting, admin, security, infra

features.description: The check command named in ARCHITECTURE.md §5 fails on deliberately broken code and passes on good code.
steps: Break one file the check should cover - delete a variable something else reads.
Run the check command from its declared working directory.
Confirm it exits non-zero AND names the file and the line.
Run it again and confirm it exits zero.

evidence.command: cd /d D:\Data\Folders\My_AI_Projects\OnoBase\onobase_App  then  npm run typecheck  (three stages: tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit, tsc -p tsconfig.electron.json --noEmit, tsc -p tsconfig.preload.json --noEmit, then echo typecheck: 0 errors). Break test: src\utils\colors.ts line 3 renamed MODULE_COLORS to MODULE_COLORS_BROKEN, npm run typecheck, then the rename undone and npm run typecheck again. Hook: git config core.hooksPath .githooks, then git add -A and git commit with the break in place, and again with it undone.
evidence.output:
GOOD CODE: typecheck: 0 errors. All three stages ran - app, electron and preload. The electron and preload stages had never been reached before, because the app stage had always failed first and stopped the && chain.
BROKEN CODE: 10 errors in 2 files, and NO 'typecheck: 0 errors' line. Files and lines named: src\App.tsx lines 31, 160 and 522, and src\utils\colors.ts lines 50 and 55. It followed the reference out of colors.ts into App.tsx, which is what proves it reads the project and not one file.
RESTORED: typecheck: 0 errors.
GIT POINTED AT THE HOOK: git config --get core.hooksPath printed .githooks.
HOOK REFUSED BROKEN CODE: 'pre-commit: FAILED (exit 2) - npm run typecheck', the 10 errors listed, 'Commit refused.' Nothing was committed and --no-verify was not used. The (exit 2) is the check command's exit code carried up by npm, not the hook's own - the hook's own code was not captured.
HOOK ALLOWED CLEAN CODE: the hook ran npm run typecheck, it passed, the commit was ALLOWED. Commit 7c8e26e on dev, pushed. Both directions of DOCKING.md 5c seen on the same day.
Run by Rehan, 09-20-2026, Windows PowerShell 5.1. Ten pre-existing type errors in Onobase had to be fixed first; they are listed in the evidence file. Full record at evidence\F001.txt.

features.description: hooks/block-destructive.ps1 refuses a force push and a deploy command, and stays silent on a normal push.
steps: Run block-destructive.ps1 -Command 'git push origin main' - expect NO output, exit 0.
Run block-destructive.ps1 -Command 'git push --force origin main' - expect a reason, exit 1.
Run block-destructive.ps1 -Command 'vercel deploy --prod' - expect a reason, exit 1.
